newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court releases two in security scandal case.
newsitem.headline: Turk court releases two in security scandal case.

text.p: A Turkish court on Monday released from custody two of 11 people, mostly junior police officers, being tried in connection with a security scandal that revealed ties between the state and organised crime.

State-run Anatolian news agency said the two members of a police special forces unit were set free while the case against them continued. A request for the release of the other defendants was rejected by the state security court.

The scandal erupted last November when a car crashed in the western town of Susurluk killing a wanted gangster, a top police officer and a former beauty queen. Government MP Sedat Bucak, who heads a pro-state Kurdish militia, survived the crash.
A parliamentary report spurred by the crash painted a picture of gangsters using state privileges and political connections to kill opponents, trade drugs and traffic in guns.
Interior Minister Mehmet Agar resigned after the media implicated him in the affair. He remains a government MP.
Anatolian said 10 suspects faced up to nine years in jail if found guilty under Article 313 of the penal code for forming an armed gang that threatened the security of the state.

The chief of a crack police team, Ibrahim Sahin, and the former bodyguards of MP Bucak, were among the 10. The 11th suspect could be jailed for up to four years for alleged membership in an armed gang.

In a separate case last week, the driver whose truck hit the car became the only person convicted so far. He was fined the equivalent of $43 and made to pay $720 in damages to relatives of those who died in the crash.
